Russian Drone Strikes Kyiv Apartment Building After Overnight Missile Barrage — A Russian drone struck a nine-story apartment building in Kyiv’s Solomianskyi district on Thursday morning, Nov. 12, injuring two people and causing a fire and structural damage. The strike followed an overnight ballistic missile barrage.

Russian Colonel Blown Up in St. Petersburg as Attacks on Military Figures Mount — A Russian colonel was killed in a car bombing in St. Petersburg’s Slavyanka neighborhood, the second such attack in the area in less than three months. Previous attacks have killed Russian military figures in Sevastopol and near Moscow, while an August explosion at a Moscow restaurant may have targeted Aerospace Forces chief Alexander Chaiko.

As Poland Celebrates Independence, What Holds Ukraine Together? — Poland’s survival through generations without independence offers a lesson for Ukraine. Beyond resistance to Russia, Ukrainians need a shared sense of belonging and reasons to build their future at home.

Trump Envoys Kushner and Witkoff Arrive in Moscow for Talks With Putin — Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin on ending Russia’s war against Ukraine. They are expected to travel to Dublin afterward to brief Zelensky on the outcome.

‘Putin Doesn’t Get to Choose’: Estonia Backs Kallas as EU Peace Envoy — Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal defends Kaja Kallas and António Costa as Europe’s representatives in Ukraine peace negotiations, rejecting concerns that Kallas is too critical of Russia and insisting Moscow must have no say in Europe’s choice.

Russia Pounds Kyiv With Ballistic Missiles, Fires Reported Across Capital — Russia launched an overnight ballistic missile attack on Kyiv early Nov. 12, triggering explosions, air raid alerts and fires across parts of the capital as Ukrainian air defenses responded.

‘Trump and His Envoys Are Working for Putin, Not the US,’ Top Democrats Warn — Top congressional Democrats sharply condemn Trump, Kushner and Witkoff for undermining Ukraine, pressuring Kyiv to surrender sovereign territory and promoting Kremlin demands that threaten NATO and US national security.

US Says Rubio, Wang Discussed Trilateral Summit With Russia, but China Makes No Mention — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi discussed high-level diplomacy, including a possible trilateral summit with Russia, as Washington pushes talks on peace and nuclear disarmament.

Zelensky Rules Out Donbas Concessions as Trump Envoys Arrive in Moscow for Putin Talks — As Kushner and Witkoff arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin, Zelensky rejects US pressure to surrender Donbas, demands firm security guarantees and questions Russia’s willingness to compromise.

Ireland Backs Ukraine’s 2027 Funding, Tougher Russia Sanctions and Joint Drone Production — Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin pledges to help secure Ukraine’s 2027 funding, backs tougher sanctions on Russia, while Zelensky announces Ireland’s participation in a coalition to build shelters.

EU to Blacklist 145 Russia-Linked Targets, Including 50 Banks, in New Round of Sanctions — EU ambassadors preliminarily agreed on Wednesday, Nov. 11, to add 145 individuals and entities to the bloc’s Russia sanctions lists, including 50 Russian banks and companies helping Moscow’s shadow fleet, as well those connected to hybrid warfare activities and cyberattacks. EU foreign ministers are expected to formally approve the decision on Monday, Nov. 16.

74-Year-Old Former Red Brigades Marxist Escapes House Arrest in Argentina — Leonardo Bertulazzi, a 74-year-old former senior member of Italy’s Marxist militant group the Red Brigades, has escaped from house arrest in Buenos Aires, Argentina’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday, Nov. 11. The ministry offered a $13,000 reward for information leading to his recapture. Bertulazzi had been held since 2024 pending extradition to Italy, which Argentina approved in July 2025, to serve a 27-year se

Zelensky Arrives in Dublin for European Summit Ahead of Talks With US Envoys — President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Dublin on Wednesday, Nov. 11, for the ninth European Political Community (EPC) summit and met Prime Minister Micheál Martin at Government Buildings. He said he has bilateral and multilateral meetings planned with about 20 leaders, along with a meeting on diplomacy with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. The envoys are planning to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in

SBU Confirms Ust-Luga Strike, Says Kalibr-Carrying Missile Ship Also Hit — The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) said its drones, working with other units of Ukraine’s Defense Forces, struck port, oil refining and transport infrastructure at Russia’s Ust-Luga port in the Leningrad region overnight into Wednesday, Nov. 11. According to reports, tanks were hit at the Novatek-Ust-Luga and Ust-Luga Oil terminals, causing a petroleum spill and large fires. A small missile ship that carries Kalibr and

Zelensky: Russia Seeks Freedom to Use Force, Not Genuine Security — President Volodymyr Zelensky told Denmark’s parliament, the Folketing, that Moscow’s calls for security guarantees have nothing to do with genuine security, noting that nobody has attacked Russia in decades. He also warned that Patriot interceptors Ukraine needs are being sent to the Middle East, leaving the country unable to stop most Russian ballistic missiles. His remarks came as the first trilateral talks between Moscow and

US DEA Aided Ukraine’s Probe Into Police-Protected Drug Ring, Interior Minister Says — Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said on Nov. 11 that the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) helped Ukraine expose the Khimprom criminal group by sharing operational and analytical information. The announcement follows a NABU and SAPO investigation, published Nov. 4, alleging that SBU and National Police officials helped protect the group.

Luc Chénier Marks 5 Years as Kyiv Post CEO With 20-Fold Growth in Monthly Website Views and 7-fold Growth in Digital Revenue — Free access and international digital reach underpin a strategy to fund journalism and bring Ukraine’s story to the world

Armenia Boycotts Russia’s CSTO Alliance as Putin Hosts Moscow Summit — Russia is using its final year as a chair of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) to promote closer military cooperation and a new counterterrorism strategy. But the Moscow summit comes amid a deepening crisis of confidence in the alliance. Armenia has suspended its participation, while Russia’s war against Ukraine has strained its military resources and weakened its ability to act as a regional security guarant

EXPLAINER: Why Ukraine, Russia, and US See Talks Differently — Ukraine, Russia, and the US ended two days of negotiations in Abu Dhabi with an agreement on a major prisoner exchange but different assessments of wider progress. Kyiv highlighted security and economic recovery, Moscow emphasized a broader European security framework, and Washington acknowledged that territorial disputes remain the hardest obstacle to a settlement.

Estonia, Ukraine Build Digital Tools to Track Russian War Crimes, Abducted Children — Estonia and Ukraine are developing secure digital systems to preserve evidence of Russian war crimes and help locate and return Ukrainian children abducted by Russia. Estonia’s justice and digital minister said the projects will involve protected evidence-sharing channels and digital forensic analysis. The cooperation builds on Ukraine’s experience countering Russian cyberattacks, which Estonia said is already

Russia Proposes Nonaggression Pacts With NATO Members — Russia could sign nonaggression pacts with individual NATO members and offer them additional security guarantees, a senior Russian diplomat said. The proposal comes as Moscow pushes for a broader European security framework during Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

Russia’s New Mass-Produced Cruise Missile Crammed With Sanctioned Electronics — Ukraine’s HUR reports Russia’s upgraded Geran-5 K-5K jet drone (a cheap ~$150k “small cruise missile”) contains 93+ sanctioned US/Chinese dual-use parts (e.g. Texas Instruments). Mass-produced at Alabuga (~4,000/mo), it enables low-altitude precision strikes. Recent attacks killed dozens; Trump waived related Graham Act sanctions in October.

France Fears Nuclear War as Germany Builds Long-Range Arsenal to Strike Deep Inside Russia — Paris wants Berlin to align its long-range weapons doctrine with France’s nuclear strategy as Germany expands its arsenal with weapons capable of striking deep inside Russia. French officials warn that miscalculated signals could push Europe across the nuclear threshold.

Witkoff, Kushner to Meet Putin in Moscow After Abu Dhabi Talks — US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will fly to Moscow on Nov. 12 to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, Kushner said after Abu Dhabi’s trilateral talks concluded. They are then due to meet President Volodymyr Zelensky. A Ukrainian negotiator said a new round of talks should be scheduled after those meetings.

Jet-Powered Russian Drone Slams Into Busy Market, Killing 3 in Odesa Region — A Russian jet-powered drone struck a crowded market in central Chornomorsk on Nov. 11, killing 3 people and injuring 11. The attack also damaged nearby homes and vehicles, and set a private house on fire.

Ukraine Talks in Abu Dhabi: Europe Sidelined — US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi have sparked debate over Europe’s exclusion from negotiations. While a prisoner exchange offers hope, European commentators warn that a deal favouring Moscow could threaten European security, Ukraine’s sovereignty and regional stability. They stress the need for stronger European unity, pressure on Russia and meaningful security guarantees for Ukraine.

Ukraine Sees Momentum for Deal Before New Year — Ukrainian negotiator Davyd Arakhamia says the Abu Dhabi talks created momentum for a solution before the end of 2026, despite Russia’s rigid instructions and unresolved territorial disputes. He confirmed plans for a potentially record prisoner exchange, urged a quick follow-up round, and reported progress toward wider European participation, while leaving some advances undisclosed.

Sybiha Discusses Trade With Turkey’s Top Diplomat — Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha met his Turkish counterpart Hakan Fidan on the sidelines of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, where Kyiv plans to highlight the environmental consequences of Russia’s war and push for international attention to accountability for ecocide. The minister also discussed growing bilateral ties, the Black Sea security situation and Turkey’s role in efforts to achieve a lasting peace.

Kyiv to Switch Off Outdoor Lighting Across Capital Amid Power Shortage — Kyiv will temporarily switch off outdoor lighting across the capital to conserve electricity amid widespread power shortages caused by Russian attacks on energy infrastructure. Exceptions will apply to lighting connected to public warning systems.

Russia Bridge Collapse: No Rail Connections to Komi Republic — A railway bridge across the river into Russia’s Komi Republic collapsed on Tuesday morning, derailing multiple wagons and effectively cutting off all rail connections to and from the republic. The cause remains unclear, and the Arkhangelsk regional governor declared a state of emergency after the incident.

$16M Ka-52 Feared Lost as Pilots Die Repelling Drone Attack — Russian milblogger Tumanov reported that pilots died defending St. Petersburg from a Ukrainian drone attack. Russian Telegram channels claimed a Ka-52 helicopter was lost, but Moscow has not confirmed any aircraft losses.

US Asks Russia About NATO-Like Guarantees for Ukraine – FT — Washington has asked Moscow whether it would object to US security guarantees for Ukraine resembling NATO’s Article 5. Any US commitment would require President Donald Trump’s approval. Russia is resisting European participation and a limited ceasefire as negotiations broaden into questions about Europe’s postwar security.

Kremlin Revives Old Ultimatum: Ukraine Can Join EU, But No Military Alliances — Russia has again demanded that Ukraine stay out of all military alliances, including European ones, while claiming it would accept Kyiv’s EU membership. The reported position echoes Moscow’s earlier demands for Ukrainian neutrality and restrictions on its security choices.

Russia Strikes 6 Major Power Substations Across Ukraine Overnight — Russia attacked six major power substations across Ukraine overnight on Wednesday, Nov. 11, Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskiy said. Strikes damaged power lines in numerous regions, a heating facility in Kryvy Rih and railway infrastructure in two regions. Ukrenergo reported power outages in eight regions, with the most difficult situation in Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk and Odesa regions. At least 14 people were injured.

Iran Refuses to Send Enriched Nuclear Material to Russia — Iran reiterated its refusal to send its enriched nuclear material abroad on Tuesday, including to Russia, which reportedly offered to store the material on multiple occasions during calls with Washington. While Tehran is said to possess 440.9 ⁠kg (972 lbs) of uranium enriched to above civilian grade before the US’s June 2025 strikes, it remains unclear how much of the material survived.

Fico Says Merz ‘Shouted’ at Him Over Russia Sanctions — Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico says Friedrich Merz shouted at him and threatened Slovakia’s funding during an earlier dispute over sanctions against Russia. Fico recalled the alleged call while accusing the German chancellor of “blackmail” over Ukraine financing. The latest clash concerns Germany’s threat to block the EU’s next long-term budget unless all members commit to supporting Kyiv.

Russia’s Chief Negotiator Vows to Take Back ‘Every Inch of Russian Land’ — Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large-scale prisoner exchange during talks in Abu Dhabi, Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky said, with details to be announced soon. He described European security as the central issue, reported common ground on some points, and praised US envoys while criticizing European governments.

Ukraine Expects First Gripen Jets in Early 2027, Zelensky Says — The first Swedish Saab JAS 39 Gripen fighter jets are expected to arrive in Ukraine in January or February 2027, the Ukrainian leader said on Tuesday. Kyiv is pushing to accelerate deliveries to strengthen air defenses against Russian drone attacks, including jet-powered Shaheds. Sweden has pledged up to 16 Gripen C/D aircraft, while Ukraine has separately agreed to purchase 16 newer Gripen E fighters.

FSB Claims Polish Intelligence Network in Kaliningrad Disrupted, 2 Arrests — The FSB claimed to have arrested two alleged Polish intelligence operatives accused of gathering defense-related and socio-economic information in Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave. According to the Public Relations Center, they also identified seven Polish citizens and three Russians, who were in contact with Poland’s intelligence services.

Putin Appoints 8 More Judges in Occupied Ukraine, Military Intel Says — Dmitry Minayev, who heads an FSB department linked by Ukrainian officials to a 2019 attempt to kill Kyrylo Budanov, has joined Russia’s delegation for talks with Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi.

Post-Election Surprise: Trump’s ‘Beautiful’ Deal and How to Counter It — The Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections could change the political climate in favor of Ukraine, but it does not guarantee renewed US support. Against this backdrop, a possible “beautiful” Trump-Putin deal poses new risks and requires Europe and Ukraine to develop a stronger security strategy, increase military support, and improve engagement with the US political establishment.

Ukraine Wants West to Fund 800,000-Strong Army for 10 Years After War — Ukraine is seeking long-term Western funding to maintain an 800,000-strong army after the war to deter future Russian aggression. The proposal contrasts sharply with Moscow’s demands to limit Ukraine’s military, including a 2022 proposal to cap its forces at 85,000 troops. Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi are also addressing NATO-style security guarantees and Europe’s future security architecture.

NATO Weighs Overseas Force Cuts to Focus on Russia — NATO allies are considering whether to stop requiring enough forces for a major European war and several overseas crisis missions simultaneously, Politico reported. The proposal would prioritize defense against Russia without automatically changing current deployments. It follows allied work on Baltic reinforcements and plans for deep strikes in response to a Russian attack.

Ukraine Rejects US Plan to Redraw Donbas Borders to Give Putin Symbolic Victory — Ukraine rejected a US proposal to redraw Donbas borders as a way to break the deadlock in peace talks, insisting it will not recognize Russian control over occupied Ukrainian territory. Discussions in Abu Dhabi instead focused on security guarantees and humanitarian issues, including prisoner exchanges, while Washington sought to bring European officials into the negotiations.

Second Day of Ukraine-Russia Peace Talks in Abu Dhabi Comes to an End — Ukraine, the US, and Russia concluded negotiations in Abu Dhabi, with a possible ceasefire, energy security, and Black Sea security on the agenda. The parties also discussed security guarantees and prisoner exchanges, while Europe’s role in future talks remains unresolved.

Russia's 163-Drone Assault on Ukraine Sends Missiles Into Moldova — Two Russian Banderol missiles entered Moldovan airspace during an overnight attack involving 163 drones against Ukraine. Strikes killed one person, injured over 10, damaged infrastructure, and left 135,000 consumers without electricity in the Odesa region.

Pentagon Gives ‘Green Light’ for Permanent US Base in Poland, Defense Minister Says — he Pentagon has backed Poland’s bid for a permanent US military base, but Trump must give final approval, expected in early December. Warsaw also secured a positive recommendation for its request to purchase US Tomahawk missiles.

Ukraine, South Korea Move to Repair Ties After POWs Dispute — Ukraine and South Korea are moving to normalize relations after a dispute over Kyiv's disclosure of two captured North Korean soldiers. Seoul says it remains open to humanitarian aid and support for Ukraine's reconstruction.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 10, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 10, 2026.

Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Russia’s Ust-Luga Port, Disrupts Flights — A massive overnight drone attack struck Russia’s strategic Ust-Luga port on Wednesday, sparking a fire and causing a transformer substation shutdown. Russian authorities claimed to have intercepted 150 drones across Leningrad region. The strike came as Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure disrupted electricity, heating, and water supplies in Kryvyi Rih.

Russia, Iran Partner to Counter US Arms Crackdown as European Missile Threats Grow — Russia and Iran are coordinating efforts to counter a new US operation targeting arms shipments through the Caspian Sea. According to ISW and CTP, Tehran has also abandoned its 2,000-kilometer missile-range limit, potentially expanding the threat to American military installations and NATO territory in Europe.

‘None of the Aid Reached the People’ – Russian Authorities Deny Humanitarian Aid in Oleshky — Kherson regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin said Russian occupation authorities are withholding humanitarian aid intended for civilians in Oleshky, keeping supplies in a warehouse instead of distributing them. Around 1,300 residents remain in the city, while 92 surrounding villages face serious humanitarian difficulties.

Russia Launches Massive Drone Attack on Kryvyi Rih, Damages Power and Heating — Russian drones struck critical infrastructure in Kryvyi Rih late on Tuesday, Nov. 10, leaving parts of the city without electricity and disrupting heating and water services. Residential buildings, schools, and kindergartens were also damaged.

Russia Misled US Negotiators About Territorial Control in Donbas, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russian military and intelligence officials presented false battlefield claims during Abu Dhabi peace talks. He challenged Moscow’s territorial demands, called for greater US pressure on Russia, and expressed readiness for direct negotiations with Putin.

US Army Soldier Suspected of Spying for Russia Arrested in UK — British counterterrorism police arrested a senior US Army soldier suspected of espionage linked to Russia. The serviceman, who had access to sensitive information, remains in custody as authorities investigate.

Ukraine Reports Russian Order to Destroy Bridges Over Dnipro River — Russia has recently struck several bridges that cross the Dnipro River, particularly in Kyiv, without being able to bring them down. A Ukrainian military commander says that Moscow has given the order to destroy all the bridges across the waterway.

Ukraine, Russia Discuss Exchange of Up to 1,500 Prisoners Each as Moscow Raises Territory Issues — Ukrainian and Russian negotiating teams discussed exchanging either 1,000 or 1,500 prisoners of war (POWs) each on the first day of US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10, President Volodymyr Zelensky said during a press conference in Copenhagen. The second day of talks, on Nov. 11, is set to focus on de-escalation, energy, the Black Sea and a possible trilateral leaders’ meeting. Senior US envo

South Korea Allocates $100M for Ukraine in 2027 Draft Budget as Foreign Ministers Meet to Mend Ties — Seoul has included $100 million for Ukraine in its draft budget for 2027, JoongAng Ilbo reported on Tuesday, Nov. 10, despite a diplomatic rift between the two countries over Kyiv’s public disclosure that it had handed over two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to South Korea. Half of the announced funding would go to a NATO trust fund for Ukraine, with the rest earmarked for humanitarian pro

Ukraine Working on Second Evacuation From Russian-Occupied Oleshky, Ombudsman Says — Ukraine is working to organize a second evacuation of civilians from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in the Kherson region, Ukraine’s commissioner for human rights Dmytro Lubinets said on Tuesday, Nov. 10. According to him, more residents had requested to leave for Ukrainian-government controlled territory after witnessing that the first operation worked safely. The first operation, brokered by US First Lad

Ukraine Upgrades Pluton System to Detect Mesh Modems in Russian Drones — Ukrainian defense technology company Infozahyst has announced an upgrade to its Pluton drone detection and warning system to identify mesh modems used to control Russian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The addition of mesh modems has allowed Moscow’s drones to penetrate more deeply into Ukrainian territory.

Denmark Allocates €20M to Restore Kherson Region’s Power Supply — Denmark will provide an energy package worth €20 million ($22 million) for Ukraine’s Kherson region, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Tuesday, Nov. 10, following a meeting with Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen in Copenhagen. The announcement came on the eve of the fourth anniversary of Kherson’s liberation from Russian occupation. Earlier on Tuesday, Denmark announced a new defense package worth about €645 million

Tanker Carrying Russian Diesel Abandons US-Bound Route as Trump-Putin Deal Stalls — A tanker carrying about 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel reversed course roughly 400 nautical miles off New York. Since US President Donald Trump struck a diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Oct. 9, no Russian diesel cargo has reached the US. Doubts over Russia’s export capacity are also growing.

I KNOW WHY: What Will Be Discussed at the XI Conductors of Changes Forum in Kyiv — Kyiv will host Deloitte Ukraine’s XI Conductors of Changes Forum on Nov. 19, with Kyiv Post as international partner. Under the theme I KNOW WHY, leaders from business, government and culture will debate why to invest, create and plan in wartime, how to retain human capital, and how Ukrainian companies can scale globally. Ten percent of ticket sales and partner contributions go to the Children of Heroes Charity Fo

Ukraine, South Korea Plan Talks to Mend Ties After POW Row — Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha and his South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun plan to meet in Paris to normalize relations, a diplomatic source told RBC-Ukraine. Ties deteriorated after President Volodymyr Zelensky publicly disclosed the transfer of two North Korean prisoners to Seoul. South Korea subsequently recalled its ambassador and withdrew diplomatic personnel, although contacts between the ministers continued.

Ukraine’s Inflation Hits 11% as Russian Strikes, Middle East War Push Prices Up — Ukraine’s annual inflation accelerated to 11.0% in October from 10.0% in September, as consumer prices rose 1.8% month-on-month. Core inflation also climbed to 9.7% from 8.8%, while fuel costs have risen 53.9% in the past year.

WildField Ventures Invests $750,000 in 2 Ukrainian Startups — Ukrainian dual-use fund WildField Ventures has invested about $750,000 in two undisclosed defense-tech startups. The fund plans to announce the deals by the end of 2026 and enter talks with up to five additional startups in early 2027.

Zelensky Calls First Day of Abu Dhabi Talks ‘Constructive,’ Names Prisoner Release as Priority — President Volodymyr Zelensky described the first day of trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, Nov. 10, as constructive and substantive, naming the release of prisoners as Kyiv’s priority. He said the delegations discussed humanitarian steps, security guarantees for Ukraine and the need for de-escalation. According to sources cited by RBC-Ukraine earlier on Tuesd

G7 Foreign Ministers Meet in Paris to Discuss Ukraine Support — Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers gathered in Paris on Nov. 10 to discuss continued support for Ukraine, including military assistance, energy security and peace efforts. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha joined the talks, while France placed Ukraine at the center of its G7 agenda. Ministers also addressed humanitarian assistance and international security challenges.

Italy’s 13th Ukraine Aid Package Stalls Over 1 Signature — Italy’s 13th aid package for Ukraine is awaiting Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti’s signature, preventing publication of the decree and the dispatch of assistance, ANSA reported. Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said the delay was procedural and Giorgetti supported the measure. The dispute comes as Matteo Salvini’s League presses its coalition partners to stop sending weapons to Kyiv.

Ukraine Takes First Step Toward Joining Single Euro Payment Area — Ukraine’s parliament passed a bill on joining the Single Euro Payment Area (SEPA) in its first reading on Nov. 10. The Finance Ministry says membership will speed up payments and save the Ukrainian economy €70-100 million in banking fees. The bill also raises the financial monitoring threshold and is a condition for EU and World Bank support.

Russia’s 400,000 Confirmed Troop Losses – a Detailed Breakdown — Leaked Rosstat data of death certificates obtained by hacker groups have shed light on confirmed Russian war deaths, estimated at around 450,000. The data shows the Muslim republic of Bashkortostan taking the brunt of war deaths, with eastern Ukraine’s Donetsk witnessing over half of the overall deaths since Moscow’s 2022 invasion began.

Russia Sends FSB Chief to Face Budanov at Peace Talks After His Unit Was Linked to Plot to Kill Him — Dmitry Minayev, who heads an FSB department linked by Ukrainian officials to a 2019 attempt to kill Kyrylo Budanov, has joined Russia’s delegation for talks with Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi.

Abu Dhabi Talks Cover Security Guarantees for Russia — Ukraine, Russia, and the US discussed security guarantees for Kyiv and Europe, alongside Moscow’s demands for guarantees of its own, according to a source cited by Ukrainska Pravda on Tuesday. Ukraine’s delegation insisted that the war must stop before a broader European security framework can be developed. The talks also addressed Ukraine’s postwar reconstruction.

UN Official: Russian Weapons Are Killing Ukrainian Civilians Faster Than Ever — UN official Kayoko Gotoh told the Security Council Russian attacks killed 328 civilians and injured 2,105 in September, up 85% year-on-year. October casualties remained similarly high; UN figures since February 2022: 17,968 dead, 57,713 injured.

US Urges Russia to Let Europe Join Ukraine Talks — US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will press Russia to accept direct European participation in future Ukraine peace negotiations, Politico reported on Tuesday. European officials are already holding separate consultations in Abu Dhabi, but Washington wants them involved in the main talks. The proposal adds urgency to Europe’s unresolved debate over who should represent it.

France Accuses Iran of Europe-Wide Industrial Fridge Hack — After a cyberattack hit industrial fridges across Europe and reportedly spoiled millions of euros worth of food in mid-October, France has accused a hacker unit affiliated with Tehran of responsibility. Another wave of similar cyberattacks followed weeks later against other European countries, though it remains unclear whether the two waves are related, and the perpetrator of the second wave remains unclear.

Russia Hits Epicentr K Mall in Kropyvnytskyi, 2 Injured — A Russian attack hit an Epicentr K shopping center in Kropyvnytskyi on Tuesday morning, injuring two people and starting a fire after a repeat strike. The retailer, Ukraine’s largest home improvement chain, has faced a wave of attacks since August that destroyed malls in Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Kyiv, and Kharkiv and its last major logistics hub in Khmelnytskyi.

Exclusive: Russia Preparing Strikes on Ukraine’s Food Industry, Intel Source Says — Russia is preparing attacks on Ukrainian and foreign-owned food industry facilities in Ukraine to undermine food security, damage the economy and expand its share of agricultural export markets, a Ukrainian military intelligence source told Kyiv Post exclusively.

Netherlands to Provide Naftogaz With €23M for Additional Gas Purchases — Ukraine’s gas conglomerate Naftogaz has signed a €23 million grant agreement with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), with funding from the Dutch government. The funds will go towards additional gas purchases during peak consumption periods. Naftogaz’s acting CEO said Ukraine has enough reserves for the winter, but additional supplies could provide an extra safety margin.

Zelensky: Putin Will Return in 1, 2 or 5 Years if Ukraine Gives Up Donbas — Zelensky warned that surrendering the Donbas would only give Russia time to regroup before attacking again. He said a ceasefire along current front lines, followed by negotiations, offers the fastest path to ending the war.

Neither Side May Be Able to Win This War | Stefan Korshak — Ukraine will seek a ceasefire in trilateral talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi, but Kyiv Post correspondent Korshak expects no concrete agreements. Russia’s territorial and NATO-related demands remain major obstacles, while European support remains vital to Ukraine’s defense.

Denmark Announces €643 Million Military Aid Package for Ukraine — Denmark announced its 32nd military aid package for Ukraine, worth 4.8 billion Danish kroner, as President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Copenhagen.

Bulgaria Motorway Pileup Kills 11, Dozens Injured — At least 11 people were killed and 48 injured in motorway pileups involving around 50 vehicles near Yambol, southeastern Bulgaria, amid thick fog. Bulgaria recorded the EU’s highest road fatality rate in 2025, with 71 deaths per million people.

Modified Trawler Pitched as Royal Navy Russian Sub Hunter — Norway’s Kongsberg Maritime unveiled its “Arctic Hunter” uncrewed surface vessel (USV), converted from a commercial trawler, to track Russian submarines. It is intended to operate in the Arctic and North Atlantic as part of the UK navy’s hybrid fleet concept – the pairing of uncrewed vessels with conventional warships.

Russian Drone Attack Kills 2 in Western Ukraine’s Ladyzhyn — Russian drones killed two people in the city of Ladyzhyn in western Ukraine’s Vinnytsia region on Nov. 10. The attack damaged civilian infrastructure, while energy facilities and a civilian enterprise were also hit in the region. Ladyzhyn declared three days of mourning.

Zelensky Seeks Air Defenses at Nordic Talks in Denmark — President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Denmark to discuss military assistance, air defenses, and energy infrastructure security with Nordic leaders. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen urged continued support for Ukraine amid Russian attacks on civilians and essential services. The visit coincides with US-mediated negotiations between Kyiv and Moscow in Abu Dhabi.

Russian Drone Hits Sumy Train as Crew Takes Shelter — A Russian drone struck a commuter train standing at a railway station in Sumy on Nov. 10, Ukrainian officials said. No passengers were aboard, and the crew was in shelter, preventing casualties. City authorities also reported damage to a locomotive cab and an industrial building during the morning’s attacks, as Russia continues targeting Ukraine’s rail network.

Kasparov Cancels Berlin Trip After Warnings of Assassination — Exiled Russian opposition figure Garry Kasparov canceled his appearance at Berlin Freedom Week after security experts warned of a possible Russian assassination plot. The former chess champion, previously alerted by US and Lithuanian authorities, criticized European officials for failing to counter Kremlin threats.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Aircraft Repair Facility Overnight — Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Russia’s Novgorod Oblast, which services military transport aircraft and A-50 airborne early warning planes. The extent of the damage is being assessed, but the strike could delay aircraft repairs and their return to service.
